title: Secure Millimeter-Wave Ad Hoc Communications Using Physical Layer Security
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications are highly promising to improve the capacity of modern wireless networks, while the physical layer security (PLS) techniques hold great potential to enhance the critical secrecy performance therein. By carefully exploiting the significant signal difference between the Non-Light-of-Sight (NLoS) and Line-of-Sight (LoS) mmWave links, this paper proposes a Sight-based Cooperative Jamming (SCJ) scheme to improve the PLS performance of mmWave ad hoc communications. In this scheme, each potential jammer that has no LoS link to its nearest receiver but may have LoS links to eavesdroppers is selected with a certain probability to generate artificial noise such that channel advantages at legitimate receivers can be achieved. For performance modeling of the new jamming scheme, novel and efficient theoretical approximation approaches are firstly developed to enable the challenging issue of interference distribution modeling to be tackled, and then a theoretical framework based on stochastic geometry is proposed to capture the secrecy transmission capacity behavior under the SCJ scheme. Finally, extensive numerical results are provided to illustrate the SCJ scheme under various network scenarios.

title: SecureCodeReviewer: An AI-Driven Automated Secure Code Review System with Context-Aware Vulnerability Detection
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Communication, Computing and Electronics Systems (ICCCES)
abstract: This survey examines the use of AI and machine learning in software vulnerability detection. As software becomes more advanced and complicated over the days cyber-attacks get more sophisticated and advanced, so this has become a problem, this survey examines deep learning methods like CNN, RNN & BiLSTMs, transformers like BERT and all its variations, it also examines graph-based methods like GGNNs and HAGNNs, and conventional ML methods. Key datasets include SARD, NVD, Debian Linus repositories, and Python-specific datasets have been used and examined for their advantages and disadvantages. By comparing performance metrics including accuracy, F1-score, recall, precision, and ROC, reliability is evaluated. To promote secure engineering methods, the study indicates future prospects for multimodal learning, cross-language transfer, federated learning, and integration with software pipelines. It also addresses long-standing challenges such as language reliance, dataset bias, scalability, and explainability.

title: Securing system controllers in critical infrastructures
venue: Proceedings of the Eighth Annual Cyber Security and Information Intelligence Research Workshop
abstract: Control systems are at the heart of many critical infrastructures. Malicious attacks on system controllers like SCADA (Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition) systems are serious threats to critical national infrastructures such as smart grids, nuclear power plants, or transportation systems. Analyzing and verifying the security of the control systems has increasingly become an important defense mechanism. This paper presents an approach that facilitates a semi-automated security system verification of control systems by a novel application of model checking, a technique traditionally used for automated software verification. The proposed approach is different from typical model-checking applications in that it has the ability to uncover missing safety and security properties that should be specified to prevent catastrophes caused by malicious acts. We describe the approach by illustrating its use in analyzing a cooling reactor system controller in a nuclear power plant system. The approach is general and applicable to SCADA and other control systems.

title: Securing the Last Mile of CPS Control with Typed-Plan Firewalls
venue: Proceedings of the 6th ACM Workshop on Secure and Trustworthy Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Agentic cyber-physical systems (CPS) increasingly place planners between high-level goals and effectful tool interfaces. At this execution boundary, a planner-proposed invocation may read operational state, mutate configuration, or trigger workflows, so the system needs a deterministic admission decision and durable evidence before execution. We present typed-plan firewalls, deterministic mediation layers that normalize planner output into typed intent objects, validate tool identifiers and structured arguments against explicit policies, fail closed on malformed or unsafe steps, and emit replayable denial traces. The central design choice is to mediate the typed intent object, which binds the normalized tool identifier, structured arguments, policy obligations, policy version, and decision evidence into a single audit-relevant security object. In an evaluation conformance suite, the firewall matches expected decisions on 25/25 typed-step cases spanning disallowed tools, unsafe arguments, confused-deputy patterns, and jailbreak-style argument payloads. Across three supervisory CPS scenarios and 60 runs, the firewall records denial traces for every injected unsafe step while adding 36.70 ms mean run-level task p95 adapter latency. Layer-isolating baselines show that argument inspection materially changes the boundary: allow-list and schema-only modes block disallowed or malformed calls, yet admit unsafe arguments to allowed tools; full mediation denies them. A supplementary LLM-realization package, spanning canonical and stress suites, seven prompt variants, and 2,275 trials per model, separates planner-output stability from firewall correctness. Overall, the evidence supports a deliberately bounded claim: typed-plan firewalls provide local, auditable containment for declared unsafe tool-invocation classes in agentic CPS control planes, with prompt-injection resistance, planner reliability, and physical safety addressed by complementary assurance layers.

title: Securing the Petroleum Supply Chain Through Proof of Work Implementation
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: The petroleum supply chain in India involves various players from crude oil exploration to refined product distribution, creating a complex and competitive environment. Implementing blockchain technology offers a decentralized and immutable solution to enhance transparency, security, and efficiency across the supply chain. This study demonstrates the implementation of a Proof of Work (PoW) mechanism in the petroleum supply chain using python, defining Block and Blockchain classes, creating a Proof of Work mechanism, and simulating transactions. The experimental results, using different difficulty levels, show that increasing the number of leading zeros in the hash significantly raises computational complexity and time, thereby strengthening the blockchain's tamper-resistance. This approach ensures a reliable and transparent record of petroleum transactions from extraction to end-user delivery.

title: Security against hardware Trojan through a novel application of design obfuscation
venue: Proceedings of the 2009 International Conference on Computer-Aided Design
abstract: Malicious hardware Trojan circuitry inserted in safety-critical applications is a major threat to national security. In this work, we propose a novel application of a key-based obfuscation technique to achieve security against hardware Trojans. The obfuscation scheme is based on modifying the state transition function of a given circuit by expanding its reachable state space and enabling it to operate in two distinct modes -- the normal mode and the obfuscated mode. Such a modification obfuscates the rareness of the internal circuit nodes, thus making it difficult for an adversary to insert hard-to-detect Trojans. It also makes some inserted Trojans benign by making them activate only in the obfuscated mode. The combined effect leads to higher Trojan detectability and higher level of protection against such attack. Simulation results for a set of benchmark circuits show that the scheme is capable of achieving high levels of security at modest design overhead.

title: Security measures for the manufacture & control system
venue: SICE Annual Conference 2007
abstract: The evolution and spread of the open technology has made it easier to have interactions with other networks and has accelerated the opening of the Manufacture & Control System (M&CS). Although M&CS, which was not the target of the threat before, has come to be under the influence of various threats, has different characteristics from IT system (Information Technology). That is why it is necessary to take the security measures for M&CS, by considering the characteristics specific to it and recognizing the similarities and differences from IT system. In this paper, we will describe the points to be taken into account, in taking the security measures for M&CS.

title: See My Sea - Emotion Translation and Visualization
venue: Proceedings of the 17th International Symposium on Visual Information Communication and Interaction
abstract: "See My Sea" is an innovative project that integrates art and emotion to explore human emotions through facial expressions. Utilizing advanced facial recognition and real-time data processing, the project captures subtle emotional cues and translates them into dynamic visualizations of ocean particles. This artistic endeavor transforms transient facial movements into fluid, evolving visual patterns, mirroring the vast and ever-changing nature of the sea. Viewers engage interactively with their emotional states, influencing the visual output and fostering a deeper understanding of their inner selves.

title: Seeing and Saying Movement: Combining Skeleton Visualization and LLM Feedback for Motor Skill Coaching
venue: Proceedings of the Augmented Humans International Conference 2026
abstract: We present a near real-time kickboxing coaching system that integrates (i) side-by-side skeleton visualization of an expert and a learner, (ii) per-joint directional difference highlighting, and (iii) a hybrid comment module combining rule-based messages with large language model (LLM) output. Rather than claiming robust learning effects, this short paper frames the contribution as a design exploration of how tightly coupled visual and language-based feedback can support novice interpretation of movement errors. In a small exploratory user study (n=6; brief practice per condition), we compare three feedback modalities—avatar-only (AO), rule-based feedback (RB), and hybrid LLM feedback (HL)—and report descriptive joint-level patterns and subjective user perceptions. Although objective improvements were limited at this scale, the results suggest a movement-dependent fit between modalities (global visualization for punches; localized comments for kicks) and a consistent preference for HL. We discuss design trade-offs and limitations, including temporal alignment choices and the assumption of a single expert reference.

title: Seeing Materials in Context: An Immersive AR/XR Demo for Exploring the Interplay of Shape, Material, Colour, and Light
venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
abstract: Design decisions about object shape, material, and colour are inherently perceptual and often rely on designers’ empirical judgement, as many digital tools fragment these attributes into parameter-centric workflows that hinder reasoning about appearance in context. We present an immersive AR/XR demonstration that enables integrated exploration of the interplay between shape, colour, material, and lighting. To support immersive use in XR, where mouse-and-keyboard input is unavailable, the system employs mid-air gestures for direct, embodied interaction. Illumination is represented through a small set of perceptually meaningful lighting contexts rather than low-level parameters, enabling real-time manipulation and rapid comparison across conditions. A decoupled interaction architecture stabilises perceptual exploration despite imprecise gestural input, translating established findings from visual material perception into a hands-on tool for early-stage design exploration.

title: Self-Preserving Genetic Algorithms for Safe Learning in Discrete Action Spaces
venue: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE 14th International Conference on Cyber-Physical Systems (with CPS-IoT Week 2023)
abstract: Self-Preserving Genetic Algorithms (SPGA) combine the evolutionary strategy of a genetic algorithm with safety assurance methods commonly implemented in safe reinforcement learning (SRL), a branch of reinforcement learning (RL) that accounts for safety in the exploration and decision-making process of the agent. Safe learning approaches are especially important in safety-critical environments, where failure to account for the safety of the controlled system could result in the loss of millions of dollars in hardware or bodily harm to people working nearby, as is true of many cyber-physical systems. While SRL is a viable approach to safe learning, there are many challenges that must be taken into consideration when training agents, such as sample efficiency, stability, and exploration---an issue that is easily addressed by the evolutionary strategy of a genetic algorithm. By combining GAs with the safety mechanisms used with SRL, SPGA offers a safe learning alternative that is able to explore large areas of the solution space, addressing SRL's challenge of exploration. This work implements SPGA with both action masking and run time assurance safety strategies to evolve safe controllers for three types of discrete action space environments applicable to cyber physical systems (control, routing, and operations) and under various safety conditions. Training and testing evaluation metrics are compared with results from SRL trained controllers to validate results. SPGA and SRL controllers are trained across 5 random seeds and evaluated on 500 episodes to calculate average wall time to train, average expected return, and percentage of safe action evaluation metrics. SPGA achieves comparable reward and safety performance results with significantly improved training efficiency (55x faster on average), demonstrating the effectiveness of this safe learning approach.

title: Semantic Formative E-Assessment for Project Management Professionals
venue: 2015 4th Eastern European Regional Conference on the Engineering of Computer Based Systems
abstract: The paper presents the module for formative e-assessment in a complex learning management system. The module implements the automatic evaluation of answers to open questions and provides feedback related to further reading or joining suitable expert communities. The evaluation of the questions is accomplished using diverse ontology-related technologies and open-source tools, such as GATE, WordNet, Text2Onto, OpenNLP, Jena API, Alignment API, Protégé. A use-case scenario is offered for trainees willing to obtain a project management professional certification. The challenges of integration and optimal exploitation of such a module into a learning management system are underlined, stressing the fact that the mapping between concepts which have to be evaluated through assessment and professional competences standards has not currently a straightforward solution. Thus, we could say the system-based solution we envisioned is both technology-driven and need-driven: based on combining recent semantic technologies, it satisfies the experts' urge to provide competency-based learning aligned to well-established standards which reflect the market requirements and the trainees' need of having an intelligent tool helping them to prepare for open-questions based exams, which are currently less supported by IT.

title: Semantic Modeling and Rule-Based Evaluation of Building Chiller Plant Operation Using Brick Ontology
venue: Proceedings of the 12th ACM International Conference on Systems for Energy-Efficient Buildings, Cities, and Transportation
abstract: The operation of building chiller plants is often inefficient due to issues such as low temperature differences and high water flow rates, which are difficult to detect and diagnose in practice. To address this challenge, this study develops a semantic framework for evaluating chiller plant operation using the Brick ontology. First, the equipment and sensor points of a chiller plant are modeled as a semantic graph that defines classes, attributes, and relationships between building energy systems. Then, expert knowledge and operational experience are encoded into semantic rules, which enable automated reasoning over the knowledge graph. These rules diagnose inefficiencies such as small temperature differences by sequentially analyzing relative heat-to-flow ratios, chilled water supply and return temperatures, and terminal setpoints. The semantic model is linked to the building's operational database through unique identifiers (UUIDs), enabling real-time query execution and inference. A case study is conducted on an educational building located in Shanghai, China, where the proposed approach is applied to the actual chiller plant system. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the method in identifying and interpreting inefficient operational conditions. Moreover, the ontology-based framework not only provides a standardized representation of equipment and sensors but also enhances the interpretability and reusability of diagnostic rules across different systems. This work highlights the potential of combining Brick ontology and expert rules for semantic-driven performance evaluation of building chiller plants.

title: Semantics-preserving implementation of multirate mixed-criticality synchronous programs
venue: Proceedings of the 20th International Conference on Real-Time and Network Systems
abstract: Model-based design methodologies such as Simulink/ State-flow, that are based on the synchrony assumption, are widely used in many safety-critical application domains including avionics and automotive systems. The synchrony assumption asserts that actions (such as the execution of code) occur instantaneously. However, actual platforms obviously do not satisfy the synchrony assumption. This paper considers the problem of obtaining resource-efficient implementations of programs that are written under the synchrony assumption on actual platforms, such that these implementations execute in a manner that is semantically consistent with the execution sequences that would occur if the synchrony assumption were to hold.

title: SemanticSentinel: LLM-Based Semantic Consistency for Malicious Package Detection
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The burgeoning growth of open-source package ecosystems, exemplified by npm, underpins modern software development, yet simultaneously expands the attack surface for malicious actors. Typosquatting and obfuscation techniques represent critical vectors for injecting malware into the software supply chain. Traditional detection mechanisms, primarily reliant on lexical similarity metrics such as Levenshtein distance, struggle with semantically divergent yet functionally malicious packages, resulting in high false positive and negative rates. This paper introduces SemanticSentinel, a novel framework that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform deep semantic analysis of package metadata and code. By transcending superficial string comparisons, SemanticSentinel identifies contextual inconsistencies and malicious intent often overlooked by lexical detectors. Our empirical evaluation on a dataset of malicious npm packages demonstrates that SemanticSentinel achieves a superior F1-score of 0.93, significantly outperforming baseline Levenshtein-based approaches (F1-score of 0.68). This substantial improvement underscores the efficacy of LLM-driven semantic understanding in fortifying software supply chain security against stealthy, evolving threats.

title: Semi-automated deployment of a High-lift system on IMA using the Selective Middleware
venue: 2019 IEEE/AIAA 38th Digital Avionics Systems Conference (DASC)
abstract: This paper presents a case study concerning the implementation of a High-Lift System on an Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) platform using a system management middleware and a knowledge-based automatic instantiation process. Safety-critical avionics systems usually consist several system management functions besides the specific control functions, which contribute to high development costs. System management functions such as redundancy, signal path, and fault management could be generally constructed on generic logics. The Flexible Avionics Platform approach developed at the Institute of Aircraft Systems at the University of Stuttgart describes these logics in generic software bricks to instantiate the system management. A model and knowledge-based tool suite assists to derive the system management instantiation from an abstract high-level system architecture model. Ongoing research has introduced the Flexible Avionics Platform into the IMA environment as a selectively useable middleware called “Selective Middleware” in a partition space according to the ARINC653P4 interface specification. Consequently, a development process for the Selective Middleware has to be defined and validated by the development of an appropriate system to show the applicability in an industrial development process. Hence, this paper presents a development process for a selective Middleware, which focuses on system development aspects and gives an outlook on relevant qualification procedures. Aspects of DO-297 and ARP4754A are considered to derive the development process. Subsequently, a High-Lift System function is established on grounds of the Selective Middleware approach. This High-Lift System function is divided into two development processes of (1) the generation of the system management and IMA configuration files and (2) the development of the specific control functions.

title: Semiotic Translation in Sustainable Design: Constructing a Metaphorical System for Panda Ecological Concepts in Intelligent Exhibition Design
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Computer Technology, Digital Media and Communication
abstract: Against the backdrop of intensifying global ecological crises, intelligent exhibition technologies offer new pathways for disseminating sustainability concepts. This study focuses on the giant panda and its associated ecosystems (bamboo/forest/water/circulation), integrating Peirce's semiotic triad with ecosystem metaphor theory to construct an “ecological symbol-intelligent technology-metaphorical communication” framework. Through a three-level translation strategy (iconic, indexical, symbolic), ecological elements are transformed into intelligent exhibition symbols. Leveraging AR/VR, sensor interactions, and real-time data visualization technologies, a three-tier metaphorical system (formal-relational-ethical) is established. The study further proposes functional modeling to clarify this process. This model aims to significantly enhance audience understanding of sustainability principles and behavior transformation intentions, providing a methodological paradigm for intelligent cross-cultural translation of ecological symbols.

title: Senescence: An Age-Based Character Simulation Framework
venue: 2015 19th International Conference on Information Visualisation
abstract: The paper presents the development and initial validation of the Senescence character framework, a simulation tool that can be used for rigging muscle deformer-based humanoid characters, with support for age. The senescence framework allows the user to rig any bipedal 3D character and manipulate skeleton and muscle parameters in order to render the age of the character realistically. The framework was developed using Python, Maya Embedded Language and PyQt. A study with 100 subjects was conducted to determine whether participants were able to perceive the age of the characters simulated with the Senescence framework. Findings show that while subjects were able to perceive age differences, they were not able to identify the age of the simulated characters with high level of accuracy. Results also show that subjects with animation expertise were able to identify the age of the characters more accurately than subjects without animation experience.

title: SenseKit: A Modular Approach to Human-Data Interaction in the Workplace
venue: Proceedings of the Twentieth International Conference on Tangible, Embedded, and Embodied Interaction
abstract: Modern workplaces increasingly rely on embedded sensors to monitor environmental conditions, yet these systems often operate opaquely—collecting data without user awareness, understanding, or agency. As a result, office workers lack the ability to interpret or act on data that impacts their well-being. To address this gap, we present SenseKit: a modular sensing system grounded in Human-Data Interaction principles of legibility, agency, and negotiability. SenseKit combines stationary modules that monitor environmental variables (air quality, light, noise) with wearable components that track personal well-being data (heart rate, activity, sleep). In a one-day field deployment, two office workers used SenseKit to explore their own environmental and physiological data in real time. The system supported situated reflection, encouraged environmental adjustments such as changing seats or opening windows, and prompted broader interest in how sensor feedback could guide healthier work routines. These findings illustrate how HDI-aligned, modular systems can support data-driven awareness and action.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Stock Prices and News Headlines Using the MCDM Framework
venue: 2022 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Speech Technology (AIST)
abstract: In the 21st century, the speedy progress in digital data procurement has led to the fast-growing amount of data kept in the database, data warehouses, or other data storehouses. The main reason behind this is that it provides a fast spreading of information and increases technology usage. The stock market is one of the utmost competitive financial markets where traders want to compute financial capacities with low latency and high output. In this study, we introduced an unsupervised MCDM-based Grey Relational analysis (GRA) model that targets giving appropriate sentiment tags to the news headlines and predicting the forthcoming stock prediction. To check the proposed model's applicability, we used INFOSYS and WIPRO datasets, which give satisfactory results over the proposed model. We recorded an accuracy of around 87%. We utilize a practical GRA model approach to evaluate and recommend the finest share stocks based on news headlines from multiple web sources. Our system's performance is evaluated using real-time data from WIPRO and INFOSYS.

title: SGFR-Track: Uncertainty-Gated Spectral Feature Restoration for Online Multi-Object Tracking
venue: Proceedings of the 2026 International Conference on Multimedia Retrieval
abstract: Online multi-object tracking (MOT) often fails under frequent occlusions and non-linear motion because corrupted temporal appearance embeddings introduce association ambiguity and identity switches (IDS). Existing methods mainly improve backend association, but largely overlook the direct restoration of degraded features themselves. We propose SGFR-Track, an uncertainty-gated spectral feature restoration framework for online MOT. The key idea is to treat occlusion-induced feature corruption as high-frequency temporal noise and restore discriminative appearance cues before association. To this end, we first introduce a Gating Funnel based on the Bidirectional Matching Margin (BMM) to diagnose tracklet ambiguity online and activate restoration only for high-risk tracklets, improving efficiency while avoiding over-smoothing of reliable samples. We then design a Spectral-Guided Feature Restoration (SGFR) module that performs adaptive denoising in the frequency domain via the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT). Extensive experiments under the unified BoxMOT framework on DanceTrack, MOT17, and MOT20 show that SGFR-Track consistently improves overall tracking performance while preserving real-time speed. These results demonstrate that spectral signal processing offers an effective and physically interpretable direction for enhancing feature robustness in online MOT.

title: ShadAR: LLM-driven shader generation to transform visual perception in Augmented Reality
venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) can visually transform a user’s world by rendering virtual content on top of reality. However, developing such AR apps and visualizations remains a complex process that requires an understanding of computer vision and programming skills. We present ShadAR, an AR prototyping pipeline that enables real-time creation of small AR visualizations and applications using large language models (LLMs) and object detection. ShadAR allows users to express their visual intent (e.g., pixelate every person around me) via natural language, which is interpreted by an LLM to generate corresponding shader code. This shader is then compiled in real-time and applied to the passthrough video stream.

title: Shield Decentralization for Safe Reinforcement Learning in General Partially Observable Multi-Agent Environments
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Autonomous Agents and Multiagent Systems
abstract: As reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used in safety-critical systems, it is important to restrict RL agents to only take safe actions. Shielding is a promising approach to this task; however, in multi-agent domains, shielding has previously been restricted to environments where all agents observe the same information. Most real-world tasks do not satisfy this strong assumption. We discuss the theoretical foundations of multi-agent shielding in environments with general partial observability and develop a novel shielding method which is effective in such domains. Through a series of experiments, we show that agents that use our shielding method are able to safely and successfully solve a variety of RL tasks, including tasks in which prior methods cannot be applied.

title: Short encodings of planar graphs and maps
Short Paper: AI-Driven Disaster Warning System: Integrating Predictive Data with LLM for Contextualized Guideline Generation
venue: Proceedings of the 11th International Conference on Networking, Systems, and Security
abstract: Early warning systems are the backbone of disaster management, but traditional systems often send static alerts with no personalized advice. This work investigates an AI-powered disaster warning system using predictive analytics and LLMs to design personalized recommendations over efficient response strategies. This system ensures that real-time information on context-specific and geographically relevant preparedness is tailored to the needs of varied populations. It was built using the LangChain framework and features an architectural composition with a predictive layer in disaster monitoring and an advisory layer for proactive safety guidelines. It integrates current weather conditions with advanced machine learning algorithms to enhance disaster prediction and utilizes LLMs in constructing customized actions, hence streamlining emergency messaging with enhanced clarity and relevance. Among the tested models, it turned out that the Gemini Pro LLM is the most effective, consistently generating outputs appropriate in context and accurate. Analysis under different temperature settings demonstrated the ability of the model to maintain high precision on various types of crises. The findings indicate that this approach can transform traditional early warning systems into more adaptive, user-centered frameworks, hence enhancing disaster management practices.

title: ShoulDex: A Panel-Woven Textile Sensing System for Rotator Cuff Rehabilitation
venue: Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing
abstract: Accurate joint angle monitoring is critical for effective rotator cuff (RC) rehabilitation. While textile-based stretch sensors provide flexibility and comfort for wearable applications, integrating them reliably into fabric-based systems remains challenging. We present a panel-guided sensor embedding approach that utilizes modified garment patterns to secure stretch sensors along predetermined pathways. Based on this method, we developed ShoulDex, a soft textile system for RC rehabilitation that integrates machine learning-driven feedback. Preliminary demonstration shows distinct signal patterns across key shoulder movements (abduction, flexion, and rotation). And a LSTM-based regression model achieves a mean RMSE of 2.95 degrees for joint angle estimation. ShoulDex provides a promising solution to support unsupervised, home-based rehabilitation with real-time, interpretable feedback.

title: Shyper: An embedded hypervisor applying hierarchical resource isolation strategies for mixed-criticality systems
venue: 2022 Design, Automation & Test in Europe Conference & Exhibition (DATE)
abstract: With the development of the IoT, modern embedded systems are evolving to general-purpose and mixed-criticality systems, where virtualization has become the key to guarantee the isolation between tasks with different criticality. Traditional server-based hypervisors (KVM and Xen) are difficult to use in embedded scenarios due to performance and security reasons. As a result, several new hypervisors (Jailhouse and Bao) have been proposed in recent years, which effectively solve the problems above through static partitioning. However, this inflexible resource isolation strategy assumes no resource sharing across guests, which greatly reduces the resource utilization and VM scalability. This prevents themselves from simultaneously fulfilling the differentiated demands from VMs conducting different tasks. This paper proposes an efficient and real-time embedded hypervisor “Shyper”, aiming at providing differentiated services for VMs with different criticality. To achieve that, Shyper supports fine-grained hierarchical resource isolation strategies and introduces several novel “VM-Exit-less” real-time virtualization techniques, which grants users the flexibility to strike a trade-off between VM's resource utilization and real-time performance. In this paper, we also compare Shyper with other mainstream hypervisors (KVM, Jailhouse, etc.) to evaluate its feasibility and effectiveness.

title: Sign Language Recognition and Translation to Text and Audio for Divyang Communication as A Microservice
venue: 2025 International Conference on Electronics and Computing, Communication Networking Automation Technologies (ICEC2NT)
abstract: Communication blocks create major limitations for people who have hearing and speech disabilities when they try to communicate outside their personal circles. Researchers have developed a present-time sign language recognition platform which converts hand movements into written text and spoken words to make hearing-impaired users understand people who do not know sign language. Hand features can be extracted through Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in a system that operates with high accuracy to detect hand gestures. The system uses OpenCV-based skin segmentation and fuzzy c-means clustering methods for improving both gesture tracking and classification functionalities. The research investigates the recognition capabilities of American Sign Language (ASL) and Indian Sign Language (ISL) because they are commonly used by signers globally. The established model operates at an 88% success rate for transforming sign language signals into spoken text. The system benefits people with disabilities yet extends its functionality to human-computer interaction interfaces, gesture-controlled automation systems, and assistive technologies. This research combines deep learning approaches to create a solution connecting the deaf and mute community to standard communication through an accessible solution for sign language interpretation across realworld environments.

title: Sign Language To Speech Translation
venue: 2026 International Conference on Emerging Technologies and Future Innovations (ETFI)
abstract: Sign Language is the important means of communication for the people with speech and hearing aid, but still it is not accessible by majority of the population because it lacks the interpretation in everyday conversation. This study presents a real time sign-language translator that combines the Computer Vision and the Deep Learning concepts to reduce this gap. The architecture combines MediaPipe-based hand tracking with a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) architecture to perform feature representation and learning of gesture sequences. Preprocessed video frames will be captured by the webcam and this frames will be given to the model to predict the whole sentence instead of the single alphabet letters. The generated output will be given in the format of converted text and will be given to the Text-to-Speech model, so that we can also have Speech as a output. Experimental testing verifies that the suggested technique is able to process dynamic sequences of gestures, thus enhancing natural sign-to-sentence translation over conventional static models. This research advances the development of an intelligent real-time aid system improving hearing-impaired inclusiveness.

title: SignGlass: First-Person View Comprehensive and Generalizable ASL Translation Using Wearable Glass
venue: Proceedings of the 38th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology
abstract: Communication barriers between Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) individuals and hearing individuals remain a major challenge, highlighting the need for technologies that enable seamless sign language interpretation. However, current American Sign Language (ASL) recognition and translation systems face key limitations, including poor portability, complex usage settings, incomplete capture of essential components, and weak generalization, reducing practicality and user acceptance. To address these challenges, we present SignGlass, the first smart glasses equipped with three wearable cameras for comprehensive capture of both manual and non-manual ASL markers, supported by advanced algorithms for real-time recognition and translation into English. Specifically, SignGlass integrates a jitter-aware spatio-temporal attention mechanism for robust recognition of hand movement patterns. Complementing this, a dual-camera, temporally-aware facial module captures the subtle facial expressions essential for ASL comprehension. To support diverse signing styles across individuals, we further introduce a cascaded data augmentation strategy to improve model generalization. In a user study with 14 Deaf participants, SignGlass achieved high translation accuracy and was well-received, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging communication gaps. This work highlights the promise of multi-camera wearable systems in advancing ASL translation and promoting more accessible communication.

title: Simulated Ensemble Performance Partners: Exploring the Integration of Generative AI and Virtual Reality for Collaborative Rehearsals
venue: Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing
abstract: Ensemble musical performances demand both technical precision — such as exact fingerings, intonation, and tempo—as well as higher-order skills such as active listening, real-time responsiveness, and emotional expression. This study explored the ways that generative AI and VR could be used to facilitate this complex interplay of cognitive and expressive demands. We conducted a needs-finding pilot study with four advanced viola students who rehearsed in a gallery-style virtual concert hall accompanied by a smartphone-based AI partner. Post-rehearsal interviews underwent thematic analysis to identify key system requirements for simulating an effective ensemble partner. Three core needs emerged: (1) faithful interpretation of score arrangements to support expressive nuance, (2) adaptive sensory feedback to enhance VR immersion, and (3) pre-rehearsal exchange of emotional intent. The insights gained in this study could guide the development of AI/VR systems aimed at augmenting ensemble practice, supporting iterative rehearsal in immersive environments that complement human musicianship.

title: Simulation of PKI-enabled communication for identity management using CyberCIEGE
venue: 2010 - MILCOM 2010 MILITARY COMMUNICATIONS CONFERENCE
abstract: CyberCIEGE is a sophisticated network security simulation packaged as a video game and used by educators around the world to enhance information assurance education and training at universities, community colleges, within the DoD, and in other government agencies. The CyberCIEGE game engine was recently expanded to include Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) features including certification authorities, selection of installed roots and cross certification. CyberCIEGE Virtual Private Network (VPN) gateways, VPN clients and email clients were then extended to incorporate the new PKI features. CyberCIEGE PKI abstractions are described in terms of player configuration choices and the consequences of these choices on network management and vulnerabilities. The CyberCIEGE game engine modifications include modeling of chains of trust and risks of cross certification schemes. The benefits of these enhancements include coherent integration of identity management technologies, ranging from the human interface through to the supporting distributed infrastructure, into scenarios. Benefits also include support for recent new scenarios focused on the PKI infrastructure, identity management, or both; and the ability to tie both identity management and PKI to concepts of identification, authentication, provenance, and access control.

title: Simultaneous Trajectory Optimization and Force Control with Soft Contact Mechanics
venue: 2020 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
abstract: Force modulation of robotic manipulators has been extensively studied for several decades but is not yet commonly used in safety-critical applications due to a lack of accurate interaction contact modeling and weak performance guarantees - a large proportion of them concerning the modulation of interaction forces. This study presents a high-level framework for simultaneous trajectory optimization and force control of the interaction between manipulator and soft environments. Sliding friction and normal contact force are taken into account. The dynamics of the soft contact model and the manipulator dynamics are simultaneously incorporated in a trajectory optimizer to generate desired motion and force profiles. A constrained optimization framework based on Differential Dynamic Programming and Alternative Direction Method of Multipliers has been employed to generate optimal control inputs and high-dimensional state trajectories. Experimental validation of the model performance is conducted on a soft substrate with known material properties using a Cartesian space force control mode. Results show a comparison of ground truth and predicted model based contact force states for multiple Cartesian motions and the validity range of the friction model. The proposed high-level planning has the potential to be leveraged for medical tasks involving manipulation of compliant, delicate, and deformable tissues.

title: SiPhyR: An End-to-End Learning-Based Optimization Framework for Dynamic Grid Reconfiguration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Smart Grid
abstract: Distribution grids are rapidly transforming with increasing penetration of distributed renewable generation, storage, and electric vehicles. These devices introduce new dynamic signatures including intermittency and changing demand patterns. To maintain a safe and reliable power grid, new operating paradigms are required for fast and accurate decision making. It is in this regard that we leverage machine learning for grid operations. We propose SiPhyR, a physics-informed machine learning framework that accomplishes end-to-end learning-based optimization for distribution grid reconfiguration. The reconfiguration problem optimizes the topology of the grid and power flows from distributed devices to reduce line losses, improve voltage profiles, and increase renewable energy utilization. To address the computational complexities of NP-hardness of binary decision variables, we propose a physics-informed rounding approach that explicitly embeds discrete decisions into an end-to-end differentiable framework. This enables Grid-SiPhyR to learn to simultaneously optimize grid topology and generator dispatch with certified satisfiability of safety-critical constraints. Our results are shown on three canonical distribution grids.

title: SketchAI: A "Sketch-First" Approach to Incorporating Generative AI into Fashion Design
venue: Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
abstract: Generative AI technologies are increasingly being incorporated into creativity support tools. However, most generative AI tools rely on text-based prompting, requiring users to translate visual ideas into linguistic descriptions. This approach is misaligned with the sketch-driven workflows of creative professionals. To address this gap, we introduce SketchAI, a novel sketch-first interface for diffusion models that allows practitioners to use real-time sketching on a tablet computer to guide model outputs. Through a qualitative study with 29 fashion design apprentices, we explored the interface’s potential impacts on creative workflows. While some participants identified use cases where SketchAI streamlined routine tasks, others expressed concerns about its potential to undermine creative agency and exploration. These findings unearthed hidden complexity: while generative AI can support some aspects of creativity, its core capabilities may challenge the central identity of creative practitioners. While SketchAI does not resolve this problem, it does take a meaningful step towards reconciliation.

title: SkillNet: Human Actions Assessment via Human-AI Collaboration
venue: ACM Trans. Multimedia Comput. Commun. Appl.
abstract: Intelligent human motion analysis is essential for developing next-generation IoT and AR/VR systems that enable automated, interpretable, and fine-grained performance assessment. Motivated by the need for real-time, explainable, and transferable skill evaluation, we propose a wearable sensing framework to assess human performance by tracking skill progression and minimizing injury risk. We use live badminton gameplay and workout exercises as representative use cases, where motion dynamics, postural stability, and limb coordination are critical to success. Both activities demand optimal posture and synchronized limb movements, while improper actions or suboptimal technique can lead to decreased performance and higher injury susceptibility. We introduce SkillNet, a multi-task learning framework that extracts shared representations across all limbs while preserving limb-specific motion signatures. The architecture employs task-specific regressors to detect subtle inter-limb dissimilarities and distinctive traits, enabling collective inference in a body sensor network (BSN) environment. To holistically measure performance, we formulated a weighted performance indicator (PI) that fuses AI-driven scoring with domain-expert evaluations, providing a robust metric for both qualitative and quantitative assessment. We evaluate SkillNet on three diverse datasets Badminton Activity Recognition (BAR), Multi-Modalities Dataset of Sports (MMDOS), and Daily and Sports Activities (DSADS) capturing a broad spectrum of motion types and skill intensities.
